Some prose belongs in more than one document: an installation section shared by a README and a website, a changelog written once and shown twice, a snippet that lives in a file outside the project.
Copying it means keeping the copies in step, and forgetting to.

`external` includes it instead.
Point the shortcode at a file or a URL and its content is parsed and dropped in, whole or by the section, div, or line range you name.

## Installation

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

Or install it from your editor with [Quarto Wizard](https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-wizard):

::: {.btn-group role="group" aria-label="Quarto Wizard installer options"}

[Visual Studio Code](vscode://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Visual Studio Code using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[Positron](positron://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Positron using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[VSCodium](vscodium://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in VSCodium using the Quarto Wizard extension."}

:::

## Quick start

The whole file:

```markdown
{{{< external notes.qmd >}}}
```

One section of it, by the identifier of its heading:

```markdown
{{{< external notes.qmd#release-notes >}}}
```

A slice of it, by line number:

```markdown
{{{< external notes.qmd#L10-20 >}}}
```

::: {.callout-important}
The shortcode has to sit on a line of its own, with a blank line above and below.
It produces blocks rather than inline content, and Quarto will not place it correctly otherwise.
:::

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every option, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for each of them rendered.

## Where it works

Every output format.
The content is parsed into the document before any writer runs, so what you include behaves like anything you typed.

::: {.callout-warning}
Including content from outside the project trades reproducibility for reuse.
A document that reads a URL is only as stable as that URL, and no longer builds the same way offline or a year from now.
:::

Code cells in the included file are not executed, in any format.
